fix(chart): correct ServiceAccount namespace in ClusterRoleBinding

Update the clusterrolebinding.yaml to use
`{{ include "local-path-provisioner.namespace" . }}` so the
ClusterRoleBinding correctly references the ServiceAccount in the
intended Namespace when `namespaceOverride` is set.

The `namespaceOverride` feauture was added in the commit 772344504a9b
("feat: add ability to set custom namespace"), but the namespace of
the ServiceAccount subject in the ClusterRoleBinding was not updated
accordingly. As a result, it continued to use
`{{ .Release.Namespace }}`, causing permission errors when a custom
namespace was specified.

fix: qualify image references to avoid short-name resolution issues

Unqualified image references like `rancher/local-path-provisioner` and
`busybox` are ambiguous on runtimes that enforce fully-qualified names
(CRI-O with short-name-mode=enforcing, the default on RHEL/Fedora).
They also resolve to docker.io implicitly, exposing clusters to Docker
Hub anonymous pull rate limits (100 pulls/6h/IP).

Prefix all image references with their explicit registry:
- rancher/local-path-provisioner → docker.io/rancher/local-path-provisioner
- busybox → docker.io/library/busybox

Affected files:
- deploy/local-path-storage.yaml
- deploy/provisioner.yaml
- deploy/example-config.yaml
- deploy/chart/local-path-provisioner/values.yaml
- deploy/chart/local-path-provisioner/README.md

Fixes #571, related to #569.

Co-Authored-By: bejaratommy <tommy@bejara.net>

helm: make debug logging configurable via values

Add a `debug` value (default: false) to the Helm chart so that debug
logging can be enabled or disabled without forking the chart. The
`--debug` flag is now conditionally included in the container command
based on this value.

Fixes #556

fix: validate helper pod template to prevent privilege escalation via ConfigMap injection

An attacker with ConfigMap edit permission in the local-path-storage
namespace could inject privileged securityContext, hostPath volumes, or
lifecycle hooks into the helperPod.yaml template. The provisioner would
then create a privileged helper pod on the next PVC operation, granting
root-level node access and enabling theft of ServiceAccount tokens from
other pods on the same node.

Add allowlist-style validation in loadHelperPodFile() that rejects
security-sensitive fields: securityContext, volumes, volumeMounts,
initContainers, ephemeralContainers, host namespaces, nodeName,
serviceAccountName, envFrom, env.valueFrom, lifecycle hooks, and
probes. Validation runs at both startup and hot-reload paths.

Add --allow-unsafe-helper-pod-template flag for deployments that
intentionally need privileged templates (e.g., XFS quota).

Signed-off-by: Derek Su <derek.su@suse.com>

fix: relax helper pod template validation to allow security hardening fields

The blanket ban on securityContext rejected both dangerous and legitimate
hardening configurations, preventing templates with runAsNonRoot,
readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities drop, fsGroup, etc.

Replace the blanket securityContext rejection with targeted field-level
checks that only block privilege escalation vectors:

Pod-level securityContext:
- Reject runAsUser: 0 (root)
- Reject runAsGroup: 0 (root)
- Reject sysctls
- Allow runAsNonRoot, runAsUser (non-zero), fsGroup, seccompProfile, etc.

Container-level securityContext:
- Reject privileged: true
- Reject capabilities.Add (e.g. SYS_ADMIN)
- Reject allowPrivilegeEscalation: true
- Allow runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities.Drop, etc.

All other existing restrictions remain unchanged (volumes, volumeMounts,
initContainers, host namespaces, nodeName, serviceAccountName, envFrom,
env.valueFrom, lifecycle hooks, probes).

Also fix kustomize image name matching in e2e tests: update image name
from rancher/local-path-provisioner to docker.io/rancher/local-path-provisioner
to match the fully qualified image references in deploy YAMLs.
